LESSON: WRITING 5.4.1 CREATIVE WRITING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.4: Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing, part of Strand 5 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why do you enjoy listening to stories? 2. Why is it important to plan our composition? 3. How can you write an interesting composition?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. describe the parts of a narrative composition in preparation for writing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. organise thoughts fluently, clearly and precisely in a coherent paragraph for self- expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. create a narrative composition of about 60-80 words for self-expression,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. realise the role of creativity in writing for different purposes.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. describe the parts of a narrative composition in preparation for writing,

   Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. organise thoughts fluently, clearly and precisely in a coherent paragraph for self- expression,

   Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. create a narrative composition of about 60-80 words for self-expression,

   Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. realise the role of creativity in writing for different purposes.

   Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. plan a composition with peers, then write a draft and present it to the whole class,

2. use similes to make their compositions interesting,

3. create their own similes and use them in their composition,

4. write a narrative composition of about 60-80 words and incorporate similes,

5. rearrange jumbled up sentences from an oral narrative into coherent paragraphs,

6. listen to a narrative on radio or television and rewrite it in their own words,

7. watch and dramatise a story related to the theme (could be from a digital device), 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. plan a composition with peers, then write a draft and present it to the whole class,
2. use similes to make their compositions interesting,
3. create their own similes and use them in their composition,
4. write a narrative composition of about 60-80 words and incorporate similes,
5. rearrange jumbled up sentences from an oral narrative into coherent paragraphs,
6. listen to a narrative on radio or television and rewrite it in their own words,
7. watch and dramatise a story related to the theme (could be from a digital device), 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 5.4.1 Creative Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: This is developed as the learner works with peers in writing a composition and

presenting it in class.

● Digital Literacy: It is developed as the learner is able to use digital devices to access and share information online.

Values:
● Love: This is enhanced as the learner interacts when working collaboratively.

● Responsibility: This is developed as the learners takes a positive initiative in writing a composition.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Lifestyle and Communicable Diseases: Sensitisation on this issue is achieved as the learner writes compositions based on the

theme Balance Diet.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of writing a narrative to their learning in Kiswahili and French.
